messages:
Maya (product): Quick sync — we need ironed-out launch criteria for dedicated capacity flow control: reserved pool sizing, quota modes, burst windows, and autoscale gating. Main goals: predictable tail latency, clear customer guarantees, and fast operator controls. Who can help scope priorities for the quarter?

Leon (eng): I can. Biggest tradeoff is exposing soft quotas to customers vs risking noisy neighbors. We should define exact behavior for soft vs hard quotas and what signals trigger fallback.

Priya (eng-sre): My suggestion: soft = token-bucket throttling with a short grace/refund window; hard = immediate 429s and session termination. Add automatic fallback routing to a compatible hosted/downgraded model on hard preempt. Key metrics: p95/p99/p999 latency, queue depth, preempt_count/min, headroom_pct.

Carlos (sales): Customers want a simple contract language — baseline reserved capacity + explicit burst best-effort. They need an easily usable SKU name. Example ask: "Reserved Plus: X baseline, Y burst (best-effort)" — with docs explaining behavior.

Mei (cs): Also frequent ask for per-route guarantees. Example: chat routes should be protected from preemption; embeddings can be best-effort. We need route-level priority overrides in the API/console.

Leon (eng): I'd propose three priorities: critical | standard | best-effort. Enforcement semantics: critical consumes reserved pool first; standard uses leftover; best-effort evicted first. Implementation approach: tag requests with session_priority, per-tenant token buckets, and KV-cache eviction by priority then LRU.

Maya (product): For an MVP launch we need: 1) API + Console config for reserved pool size + per-route priority, 2) enforcement engine with soft/hard modes (opt-in), 3) tenant observability (headroom & preempt logs), 4) pilot rollout plan with canaries. Anything missing?

Priya (eng-sre): Operator features: manual drain/reassign reserved pools, quick-evict command, and per-tenant canary flags. Also automatic fallback policy: route -> fallback_model or fallback_region. Add an operator dashboard for ongoing headroom monitoring.

Leon (eng): Example API sample for opt-in soft quotas:
{
  "reserved_pool": {"reserved_gpus": 2},
  "quota_mode": "soft",
  "route_priorities": {"/v1/chat": "critical", "/v1/embed": "best-effort"}
}
Soft mode semantics: token bucket with 10s grace. Hard mode semantics: strict counters -> immediate 429s. Preemptible sessions by tagging session_priority and evicting KV cache in priority order.

Carlos (sales): We'll need to map behavior to pricing bundles. Proposed tiers: Reserved Lite (baseline + community burst), Reserved SLA (baseline + guaranteed headroom + SLA on p95). Sales will need clear billing signals for burst usage.

Mei (cs): CS acceptance criteria: onboard 3 pilot customers exercising burst; runbook and support playbook validated; dashboard shows tenant-level burst and preempt events with alerts.

Maya (product): Draft launch checklist: 1) Spec PR with API & console mocks; 2) v1 with soft quotas + dashboard; 3) opt-in canary + pilot customers; 4) runbook + operator UI; 5) alerting rules: headroom < 10% & preempt_rate > 1/min; 6) postmortem retro plan.

Leon (eng): Timeline: v1 (soft quotas + observability + pilot) in ~6 weeks if we push per-route enforcement to v2. Hard quotas + per-route SLAs + billing tie-ins in next quarter.

Priya (eng-sre): Risks: noisy neighbors, accidental global throttles. Mitigations: feature flags, per-tenant canary, automatic fallback to hosted endpoints, and a chaos test covering preempt behavior.

Carlos (sales): I'll line up 2 pilot customers who accept soft quota semantics and gradual rollout. I'll also draft customer-facing comms clarifying "best-effort burst" implications.

Maya (product): Actions: Leon -> spec PR + sample payloads; Priya -> runbook + operator UI mock + chaos tests; Carlos -> pilot commitments + pricing SKUs; Mei -> CS playbook + onboarding checklist. Sync Wed 11am to review spec. Thanks! :rocket:

deploy-bot: Note — spec PRs touching capacity-control must include migration notes and schema changes. Branch protection enforced when PR is opened.
